role.altitude: The data warehousing specialist keeps modelling, setting standards, diagnosing problems, clarifying requirements and reviewing every change; profiling sources, typing table definitions and tests, chasing load logs and checking names by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Reviewing drafted code and tests critically
role.ambitious_version: A specialist whose warehouse flags its own failed loads and naming slips, so the time goes into models the business asks for.

tasks.short: Profile the source data, design the warehouse model, implement warehouse database structures from the model, review and merge the change, and test the structures.

steps.what: Data warehousing specialist profiles the source fields and their business meaning
Data warehousing specialist designs the warehouse model: facts, dimensions and keys
Data warehousing specialist implements the warehouse database structures: table definitions and load code
Data warehousing specialist reviews the code change and merges it
Data warehousing specialist tests the structures: row counts, keys and empty fields

tasks.design: The data catalogue profiles each source table, showing value ranges, empty fields and key candidates, so the specialist reads a profile instead of writing queries. The specialist designs the model. Table definitions, load templates and standard tests for keys, row counts and empty fields are generated from the model's metadata. The specialist reviews every change before merge, and the pipeline runs the tests on each load.
tasks.previous_blocker: Profiling, table definitions and tests were all written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Data catalogues with profiling and code generated from model metadata.
tasks.still_hard: Sources whose fields mean different things in different departments.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the grain and keys that will still work in five years.
tasks.altitude: Less typing and testing; modelling stays.

reach.learn: Whether tested tables cut report errors.

evidence.claim: Data checks run as code and documentation is generated from it.

assumptions: Boundary: from source profiling to tested structures; reports are outside.
Input contract for s1: the data catalogue, run by the data platform team, scans the connected sources nightly; about 70% of sources are connected; s1 is priced at that share.
Design and review keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of sources connected to the catalogue.
research_questions: Do load failures from wrong keys fall?

incremental.description: Data warehousing specialist keeps the code templates and generated tests current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few connected sources and unusual models; high: standard star schemas at 70% catalogue coverage.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review current models for inconsistencies, decide standards for organization, structure and nomenclature of data warehouse elements, write and agree the standard, and check new models against it.

steps.what: Data warehousing specialist reviews current models and names for inconsistencies
Data warehousing specialist decides standards for organization, structure and nomenclature of data warehouse elements
Data warehousing specialist writes the standard with examples
Data warehousing specialist agrees the standard with the data team
Data warehousing specialist checks new models against the standard

tasks.design: The naming and structure rules of the agreed standard are written as checks that the pipeline runs on every model change and on the whole repository each night. The nightly list of violations replaces reading models by hand when the standard is reviewed. Deciding and agreeing the standard stay with the specialist and the team. The standard document uses a fixed template with examples taken from the repository.
tasks.previous_blocker: Standards lived in a document nobody checked against.
tasks.enabler_now: Model repositories with automated checks in the pipeline.
tasks.still_hard: Older tables that break the standard but feed many reports.

reach.learn: Whether consistent names speed up finding data.

evidence.claim: Checks as code in a pipeline replace manual review of conventions.

assumptions: Boundary: warehouse design standards; enterprise data governance is outside.
Input contract for s1: the checks written from the current version of the standard run nightly on the model repository; the revised standard replaces them after s4.
Deciding and agreeing keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of rules that can be checked automatically.
research_questions: Do naming violations fall release by release?

incremental.description: Data warehousing specialist writes each agreed rule as a pipeline check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: rules that need judgement; high: mostly naming and structure rules that code can check.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take the reported problem, gather load logs and recent changes, diagnose the cause, fix or coordinate the fix with source owners, update the user and record the solution to provide troubleshooting support for data warehouses.

steps.what: Warehouse user reports the problem through the service desk form
Data warehousing specialist gathers troubleshooting context: load logs, job status and recent changes
Data warehousing specialist diagnoses the cause of the problem in the data warehouses
Data warehousing specialist fixes the problem or coordinates the fix with source system owners
Data warehousing specialist updates the user in the ticket
Data warehousing specialist records the solution as a knowledge item

loop.input: The ticket's notes, the cause and the fix the specialist recorded.
loop.output: A draft knowledge item: symptom, cause and fix.
loop.check: The specialist reads and corrects the draft before it is published to the knowledge base.
loop.stop: One draft per ticket; the specialist publishes or discards it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Ticket notes are free text in the specialist's shorthand.

tasks.design: Warehouse problems come in through a service desk form with the report, table and example values. The ticket automatically shows the status of the last loads, failed jobs and recent changes for that table from the orchestration tool, so the specialist does not search logs first. Diagnosing and fixing stay with the specialist. Status changes notify the user, and the service desk drafts a knowledge item from the ticket for the specialist to correct.
tasks.previous_blocker: Problems came by mail without details, and logs were searched by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Service desks linked to orchestration logs and drafting knowledge items.
tasks.still_hard: Problems caused by changes in source systems nobody announced.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which source quirk explains a strange number.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and writing; diagnosis stays.

reach.learn: Whether knowledge items let first line answer known problems.

evidence.claim: A service desk suggests category and priority, summarises tickets and drafts knowledge items for review.

assumptions: Boundary: from report to recorded solution; fixes in source systems are the source owners'.
Input contract for s2: the orchestration tool, run by the data platform team, logs every load with status and the table it fills; the change log comes from the code repository.
Users' time on the form is about what a detailed mail took and sits in s1.
Diagnosis and fixing keep their full time.

already_counted.description: Data warehousing specialist corrects drafted knowledge items.

incremental.description: Data warehousing specialist keeps the links between tables and load jobs current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: problems mostly in source systems; high: problems mostly in loads the logs explain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Clarify customer requirements, design the change, write new programs or modify existing programs, write tests, review and merge, deploy through the pipeline and confirm with the requester.

steps.what: Data warehousing specialist clarifies the customer requirements with the requester
Data warehousing specialist designs the change
Data warehousing specialist writes new programs or modifies existing programs

loop.input: The change design and the existing code in the repository.
loop.output: Draft code changes in a branch.
loop.check: The pipeline runs the tests; the specialist reads every changed line before merge.
loop.stop: The specialist merges, or writes the change by hand after two failed pipeline runs.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each change touches different transformations and business rules.

steps.what: Data warehousing specialist writes tests for the changed programs

loop.input: The change design and the code change.
loop.output: Draft tests with example rows and expected results.
loop.check: The specialist checks each expected result against the requirements; the pipeline runs the tests.
loop.stop: The specialist keeps or rewrites each test; one draft per change.
loop.why_not_simpler: Expected results depend on the business rules in the change.

steps.what: Data warehousing specialist reviews the final change and merges it
Data warehousing specialist deploys the change
Data warehousing specialist confirms with the requester that the result meets the requirements

tasks.design: A coding assistant drafts code changes and tests in a branch from the specialist's design. The pipeline runs the tests, and the specialist reads every changed line before merge. Deployment runs from the pipeline after merge instead of by hand. Clarifying requirements, designing and confirming with the requester stay with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Code, tests and deployments were all done by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistants that work in branches and deployment pipelines.
tasks.still_hard: Requirements that change once the requester sees the numbers.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what the requester actually needs.
tasks.altitude: Less typing; requirements, design and review stay.

evidence.claim: Field trials with 4,867 developers found 26% more completed tasks, more for juniors.
Sixteen experienced developers were 19% slower with AI while feeling faster; the authors call the study outdated.
A coding service offers completion, review and a background coding agent, with oversight expected.

assumptions: Boundary: changing warehouse programs for a request; new warehouses are outside.
Requirements, design, review and confirmation keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of changes the assistant drafts usefully.
research_questions: Do changes reach users sooner without more defects?

already_counted.description: Data warehousing specialist fixes drafted code that fails tests.

incremental.description: Data warehousing specialist keeps the deployment pipeline current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual changes where drafts need rework, as in the slower study; high: routine changes, as in the field trials.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
